title: OTLP HTTP backend capability discovery & health prober for dynamic exporter routing
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We currently route OTLP ingestion to a static set of downstream tracing backends (Tempo, Jaeger-compatible gateways) without probing their live capabilities. When a backend changes config (compression, envelope supported, acknowledged write semantics, TLS versions) we either fail fast or silently degrade. Batching/backpressure heuristics are brittle across backends with different supported HTTP endpoints and header expectations.

Goal: Implement an OTLP HTTP health prober and capability discovery flow that allows the trace-gateway to: 1) enumerate backend capabilities (compression, envelope, acks, max-concurrent-writes) via an authenticated capabilities probe; 2) maintain a freshness window and re-probe on errors or version changes; 3) expose capability metadata for the routing decision engine so dynamic routing can pick the most compatible exporter for each tenant and payload shape.

Acceptance criteria: 
- New endpoint probe implementation that supports HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 OTLP servers and falls back gracefully to gRPC handshake when available.
- Capability schema defined (string list) with versioning and stable fields: compression=[none,gzip,zstd], envelope=[otlp,envelope-v2], ackability=[unacked,ack-on-write,logging-ack], max_payload_bytes, tls_versions.
- Router reads capability cache and avoids sending zstd-compressed batches to backends that don't advertise zstd.
- Health prober metrics integrated to Prometheus (probe_success, probe_latency_seconds, probe_fail_reason) and dashboard drilldowns for tenant-level routing decisions.
- Unit/integration tests that run against mocked Tempo and Jaeger endpoints with permutations of capabilities.
- A small canary rollout (10% of trace traffic) behind feature flag and dashboard showing drop in failed writes and latency impact.

Design notes / trade-offs: 
- We will keep the capability schema intentionally small to avoid tight coupling. New optional capabilities can be added as extension keys.
- Storing capability cache per-tenant vs per-backend: choose per-backend cache with tenant hints to reduce memory for customers that share backends; we will record tenant-specific overrides only when backend returns tenant-scoped limits.
- Probe frequency: default 60s for healthy backends, exponential backoff up to 30m after repeated failures. Rapid re-probe will be triggered on 5xx errors in the path or schema negotiation failures.
- Authentication: use existing exporter credentials rotation flow. Prober will reuse the same credentials presented by the trace-gateway when establishing connections (token or mTLS).

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Define capability schema (open doc linked below) and wire into routing decision API.
2) Build probe client library (Go) with pluggable transport (HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, gRPC) and compression sniffing.
3) Integrate into trace-gateway: capability cache, probe scheduler, and metrics emission.
4) Add routing checks to sender: before sending a batch attempt to select compatible backend variant.
5) Create integration test harness using local mock servers (tempo-mock, jaeger-mock) that expose different capability responses.
6) Dashboard: add probe metrics and a QoS view showing percentages of write failures attributable to capability mismatch.
7) Release behind feature flag and canary for a single region.

Links: 
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/OTLP+Capability+Discovery
- RFC: https://redwood-internal/obs/rfcs/otlp-capability-discovery.md
- GH prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/trace-gateway/pull/6583
- Test harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/trace-test-harness

Notes on backwards compatibility: 
- If a backend does not implement the capability endpoint, the prober falls back to passive sniffing (observe first successful writes and extract headers) and tags the backend as legacy with conservative defaults (compression=none, ackability=unacked).

Operational runbooks: 
- On probe flapping (>5 state changes in 10m) create alert: obs.prober.flapping, runbook https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/Probe+Flapping+Runbook
- On persistent capability mismatch alerts (e.g., 5xx from Tempo due to envelope mismatch) route to Platform SRE and rollback feature flag.

Estimated effort: 5 points (~3 sprints of cross-team work including SRE, runtime, and router).
